summary:
Are you down, Carol? Your letter written at the bank sounds super down. Are you still writing? Sherry Gottlieb who owns the Change of Hobbit Bookstore and I were talking about your writing recently and when I read this letter— jeepers, Carol, can I cheer you up? For that matter, can Sherry Gottlieb cheer you up? She thinks you write neat stories. So do I. I told her you write neat let­ ters, too, and are a neat person. 

Recently a major TV network show came into Sherry’s store to do some—hehe—coverage on her tattoo, which is low in front, so to speak. Sherry wrote me, “This, see, is why they call it the boob tube.” I wrote back to congratulate her on 
getting some TV exposure for herself. I asked if the store would show. She wrote back, “No, but—” And so forth. (I think I left an h out of each heh. There’s a funny story that goes with this. I’ve been writing so hard and so long and so wea­ rily at my new novel, A SCANNER DARKLY, having gotten to page 217 and then dropped in my tracks. I wrote about 110 pages in four days. It is a somber and tragic novel, about drug addiction, but s-f, set in the future, called, you might flash on, what it is called as a sort of pun on Paul’s phrase, “... We see as through a glass darkly,” and I am saying this to explain why I am so tired, and I am so tired that I can’t type the words that explain why I am wo—see what I mean?-so tired. So I guess I’d better ring off. Or am I not on the phone? Where am I? Somebody help this man!)
